about: Written by the figure_provenance package (https://github.com/Sosnowsky/figure-provenance) each time a figure in this folder is saved, one entry per file. 'producer' is the function that drew it, a path inside the git repository 'repo' (remote 'remote') at 'commit'; 'uncommitted' lists the files that differed from that commit when it ran, other than this file and the figures it records. 'call' gives its arguments, 'called_from' the line that called it, 'command' what was run, from 'cwd'. 'purpose' is the producer's docstring. To change a figure, edit the producer and its docstring and rerun it: an edit to the file itself is lost on the next run.

coercion_2021.png.purpose:
The ABM under the three rules of Schøyen (2021) for the authority, each against the paper's analytic
answer, in the paper's notation: (a) with π frozen the families settle on q*(π); (b) the
theorem of restraint, an exogenous constraint ρ anywhere in the inefficient interval
(π_q̲, π^e_q̲) leaves the authority at π_q̲; (c) path dependence under the insurrection constraint
ρ(q), two starting ns shares ending at high and low coercion; (d) what the paper cannot show:
with finite N the high state of start A is metastable, and switches more often the fewer the
families. Okabe–Ito colours, with line style and marker shape as a second cue. The underlined
subscript q̲ is set in DejaVu Sans, since Makie's default font and LaTeX mode cannot draw it.

coercion_ensemble.png.purpose:
Six panels testing the simplest ABM of Schøyen (2021) against the stylized facts of
Schøyen, Sirnes and Andersen (2026): (a) the families reproduce q*(π) with coercion frozen;
(b) coercion is bimodal with a gap in the inefficient interval (π_q̲, π^e_q̲); (c) legitimacy
L = 1 − q dips at middle coercion; (d) collapse peaks at middle coercion; (e) coercion falls
in the years before a crackdown; (f) identical authorities end low or high depending on their
start. Panels b–e overlay a control without an inefficient interval (max C' < 2), which is
what tells the facts that need the interval (b, c) from those the authority's rule produces
anyway (d, e). Notation follows Schøyen (2021).

coercion_single_run.png.purpose:
One country's history: coercion over time with crackdowns (ticks) and collapses of the
authority (vertical lines); the ns share q against the steady state of the current coercion,
which it chases with a generational lag; and the trajectory in the (π, q) plane over the q*(π)
curve, coloured by time, so the sawtooths sit on the falling branches of q* and the rising
part between them, (π_q̲, π_q̄), is crossed only in a few fast escalations.

tourist_conformity_garden.plotly.json.purpose:
The garden figure (`fig_garden`) as an interactive Plotly figure for the note "Why did we choose Taiwan?": the same
run, lines, colours and line styles, now with a tooltip naming each destination and its visitors, zoom, legend entries
that hide or show a whole group (the winner, the 4 runners-up, the other 95, the even split), and buttons (top left, clear of Plotly's
toolbar at the top right) switching the y axis between log (as in the SVG, where 0 cannot be shown: it starts at 0.3) and linear. Colours are written as
the garden's tokens (`var(--oi-vermillion)`, …), which the page resolves for its light or dark theme; the run's parameters go in `layout.meta.caption`, which the garden shows as the caption; numbers are rounded
to 0.01 visitors to keep the file small.

tourist_conformity_garden.svg.purpose:
Popularity under conformity for the garden's note "Why did we choose Taiwan?": each of the 100 destinations'
number of visitors per year (popularity × N) over 200 years at ε = 0.1, β = 1.3, from one seed. The destination that
everybody ends up at is drawn in Okabe–Ito vermillion, the 4 others whose popularity peaked highest (runners-up that
grow for a while and then collapse) in the second colour, the rest faint, with the even split (N/D = 10) dotted.
The y axis is pseudo-logarithmic, so both the early spread around 10 and the winner's 1000 can be read. It is the
bottom row of `fig_time_evolution` with less on it (no ranking by the final year, no statistics), 200 years long
because concentration takes about 115 years at ε(β − 1) = 0.03, and in the garden's colours, drawn for its light
and its dark theme.

tourist_conformity_sweep.png.purpose:
Whether conformity (signal s_d ∝ c_d^β, β > 1) concentrates the tourists fast, and why. (a) Years
until fewer than 2 effective destinations remain, mean ± s.d. over seeds, for three ε, against
ε(β − 1) on log–log axes: the three sets fall close to one curve, since near an even split the
excess popularity grows by 1 + ε(β − 1) a year (ε enters otherwise only through the size of the
first fluctuations, logarithmically); lines are the linear-noise prediction. (b) The effective
number of destinations over 100 years at ε = 0.3 for 1000 and 10 000 tourists, with conformity
(β = 1.3, solid) and without (β = 1, dashed), as 1 / (mean Σp² over `pop_seeds` seeds; 8 seeds
left the curves visibly noisy), against the linear-noise prediction (dotted): with conformity
ten times more people only delay concentration by about a decade, without it they slow the
drift tenfold. Each panel's seed count is its subtitle, so the two titles line up.
Categorical colours in fixed order.

tourist_destinations.png.call: fig_time_evolution(runs=<Vector{@NamedTuple{visits::Matrix{Int64}, popularity::Matrix{Float64}}} (3,)>, columns=[(ε = 0.0,), (ε = 0.01,), (ε = 1.0,)], seed=1, rule=:additive, rank=:first, vmax=30, scale=<#identity>)
tourist_destinations.png.purpose:
How the chosen destinations evolve over 100 years, one column per parameter set, from the same
seed (same tastes, same first year), for one update rule (`rule`: additive, mixing, or mixing
with conformity). Top: visitors to each destination each year. Under the additive rule
(`rank = :first`) the rows of every panel are ranked by the shared year-1 visitors, so a gradient
that survives to the right is year 1's luck locked in. Under the mixing rules (`rank = :last`)
each panel is ranked by its own final popularity, since year 1 no longer predicts it, so the
panel shows the winners emerging and the losers dying out. `scale = Makie.pseudolog10`, on the
colours and on the bottom row's y axis, keeps both 10 and 100+ visitors readable when a few
destinations take most tourists. Bottom: each destination's expected visitors per year (its
popularity × N), the noise-free version of the rows above, with the 5 destinations first and
last in that ranking highlighted. Subtitles give the effective number of destinations in the
final year, how many got any visitor, and the correlation between year-1 visitors and final
popularity.

tourist_influence_sweep.png.purpose:
The ABM against the Pólya-urn prediction across the influence parameter ε, after 100 years,
mean ± s.d. over seeds. (a) The effective number of destinations of the popularity, on its full
scale from 1 (everyone goes to the same place) to D: it falls only to the strong-influence limit
D/(1 + (D−1)Σ1/t²/N), about 86 for N = 1000, D = 100, so no ε makes this model concentrate.
(b) How much of the final popularity is year 1's luck: the correlation between year-1 visitors
and the final popularity, rising from 1/√T at weak influence to 0.78 at strong.

tourist_mixing_sweep.png.call: fig_mixing_sweep(s2=<Matrix{Float64} (20, 20)>, epsilons=0.05:0.05:1.0, years=100, long=<Vector{Vector{Float64}} (3,)>, long_runs=((:mixing, 0.3), (:mixing, 1.0), (:additive, 1.0)), n_tourists=1000, n_destinations=100)
tourist_mixing_sweep.png.purpose:
Whether the mixing rule concentrates the tourists, as the effective number of destinations
1/Σp² of the popularity (1 = everyone at one place, D = an even split). (a) After 100 years
across ε: one faint dot per seed, the seed average as 1/⟨Σp²⟩, and the neutral-drift prediction
1/(1 − (1 − 1/D)(1 − ε²/N)^T); the dashed line is the most the additive rule can concentrate,
at any ε. (b) Over 5000 years on log–log axes (grey line: year 100), seed averages against their
mean-field predictions: the mixing rule drifts towards one destination on a time scale of N/ε² years, while
the additive rule freezes within a few years. Categorical colours in fixed order, black dotted
lines for the predictions.
